property_summary: Calling C.forward with calldata that targets a payable receive function must not revert and must leave the test contract's balance unchanged.
Calling forward with calldata that targets a non-payable fallback (i.e., a function that does not accept msg.value) should not revert when no Ether is sent (msg.value == 0).
Calling c.forward with arbitrary calldata that does not send Ether must not revert (reverted == false) for the original contract.
Calling c.forward(callee, data) must not revert (reverted == false).
Calling C.forward(callee, data) should not revert (reverted == false).

For any callee address, forwarding a calldata-only low-level call without sending ETH should succeed iff the callee's fallback/receive behavior treats an empty value the same; the mutant that uses call{value:0} can change how a callee's receive vs fallback is selected and thus can cause forward to revert for some calldata/callee while the reference never does.

For any callee contract and calldata, calling C.forward(callee, data) never reverts when the callee's fallback expects calldata but the mutant's use of call{value:0} can cause the call to select receive() and revert; thus the reference always succeeds (returns true) for all admissible inputs while the mutant can make forward revert for some inputs (adversarial callee that conditionally reverts in receive()).

For all callee contracts and calldata, C.forward(callee, data) never reverts when called with zero ETH (the reference uses callee.call(data) and thus will select fallback with calldata), but the mutant using callee.call{value:0}(data) can route the call to receive() and cause a revert for some adversarial callee and calldata — so the reference always returns success while the mutant can make forward revert for some inputs.

For every callee address and calldata, C.forward(callee, data) always returns (does not revert) when invoked with zero ETH; the mutant using call{value:0} can cause the call to be routed to a callee's receive() which may revert, so the mutant can make forward revert for some callee+calldata inputs.

For any callee contract and calldata, calling C.forward(callee, data) from an EOA with zero value always returns successfully (does not revert) on the reference implementation, while the mutant using callee.call{value:0}(data) can route to a callee's receive() and cause a revert for some callee+calldata inputs.
Calling forward with calldata that triggers a successful external call must not revert (i.e., the forwarded call succeeds).

property_summary: The original contract always requires the forwarded call to succeed, so calling forward reverts exactly when the forwarded call fails (i.e., reverted == (forwarded call failed)).
forward reverts whenever the low-level callee.call succeeds (i.e., reverted == success_of_callee_call).
The test asserts that calling c.forward(callee, data) must always revert (reverted == true).
Calling c.forward(callee, data) must always revert (reverted == true).

For any callee that successfully accepts a low-level call, C.forward(...) always returns normally (the call succeeds) whereas the mutant requires the low-level call to fail; thus the reference never forces failure when the callee's fallback/receive succeeds, but the mutant does for such callees.
forward always reverts if the low-level call to the callee fails (i.e., the call's success boolean must be true).
Calls to forward revert whenever the external call to the callee would fail (i.e., forward never returns successfully when the callee call would return false).
For any callee and calldata, c.forward reverts exactly when the low-level external call to callee returns false (i.e., c.forward cannot succeed if the callee call would fail).
c.forward always reverts when the low-level call it performs would return false (i.e., the call does not succeed), for any callee and calldata.
Calls to c.forward revert whenever the low-level external call it performs would return false (i.e., reverted == true implies the callee call would have returned false).

For any callee address and calldata, calling C.forward(...) always reverts (propagates failure) when the callee's fallback reverts; the mutant that drops the require allows the call to return successfully despite a failing callee.

A successful forward call must not transfer control-related ownership observable as a change in contract C's owner-dependent behavior (expressed via call success when calling a function that only the owner can successfully call).
For any inputs, calling forward(...) always reverts (i.e., it never completes successfully).
On the original contract P, forward always reverts for all inputs; assert that here.
On the original contract P, calling c.forward(callee, data) always reverts (i.e., it never completes successfully).
On the original contract P, calling c.forward(callee, data) always reverts (i.e., it never completes successfully).

For any callee and calldata, a successful forward call must NOT modify C.owner (it stays the original deployer); the mutant updates owner to callee when the external call succeeds, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any input where C.forward(...) completes successfully, the contract's owner remains the original deployer; the mutant sometimes changes owner to the callee when the external call succeeds, violating this invariant.

For every call to forward(callee, data) that completes successfully, C.owner remains the original deployer (the contract's constructor-set owner); the mutant assigns owner = callee when the low-level call succeeds, breaking this invariant for some callee addresses.

For every successful external call made through forward(callee, data), C.owner never becomes the callee (it remains the original deployer); the mutant assigns owner = callee when the low-level call succeeds, violating this invariant for some callee that has executable code.

For every call to forward(callee, data) that succeeds, C.owner remains the original deployer (the contract never changes owner based on callee); the mutant assigns owner = callee when the external call succeeds, breaking this invariant for some callee with executable code.
Calling forward must not change the caller's ownership of the contract: the owner address (observed via a public getter) is not equal to the forward caller after calling forward.

Calls to forward that succeed (do not revert) must not depend on msg.sender, i.e., if forward succeeds for some caller it must also succeed for any other caller with the same callee and data; the mutant can make success depend on caller by setting state after the call.

If calling forward(...) reverts for some inputs when invoked by this contract, then it must also revert when invoked by any other caller with the same inputs (i.e., forward's revert behavior does not depend on msg.sender).
If calling forward(...) reverts when called from this contract, then it must revert when called from any other caller (i.e., revert outcome cannot depend on msg.sender).

For any callee and data, calling forward from this contract always either reverts (reverted == true) or, if it does not revert, then calling it from any other address (simulated by checking that it does not depend on msg.sender) is not required — instead we assert that calling forward from this contract never succeeds when callee is the zero address (i.e., it reverts whenever callee is address(0)).
